drivingQuestion: Is uncertainty in vows stringent or lenient in R' Yehuda's mishna?
outcomeNote: Abaye assigns the two clauses to different tannaim

segments.he: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: סְתָם חֲרָמִים בִּיהוּדָה — מוּתָּרִין, וּבַגָּלִיל — אֲסוּרִין, שֶׁאֵין אַנְשֵׁי הַגָּלִיל מַכִּירִין אֶת חֶרְמֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים. הָא מַכִּירִין — מוּתָּרִין. אַלְמָא סְפֵיקָא לְקוּלָּא!
segments.en: However, «say the latter clause» of the mishna: «Unspecified dedications in Judea are permitted, but in the Galilee they are forbidden, because the people of the Galilee are unfamiliar with dedications allotted to the priests.» It may be inferred that where «they are familiar» with dedications allotted to the priests «they are permitted,» due to the uncertainty. «Apparently, uncertainty» with regard to vows «is» treated «leniently.»

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סֵיפָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סְתַם תְּרוּמָה בִּיהוּדָה — אֲסוּרָה, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: סְתַם חֲרָמִים בַּגָּלִיל — אֲסוּרִין.
segments.en: «Abaye said: The latter clause is» the opinion of «Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok,» not of Rabbi Yehuda, «as it is taught» in a baraita: «Rabbi Yehuda says» that «unspecified teruma in Judea is forbidden. Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says» that «unspecified dedications in the Galilee are forbidden.»
